segments.name: Agents and Infra
segments.note: Cloud and AI infrastructure, Azure, Microsoft 365 commercial cloud and server products — the engine of the quarter, up 25% YoY. Includes Azure revenue of $33,165M, up 48% YoY.

segments.name: Devices and Consumer
segments.note: Windows, Xbox, Surface devices and consumer search/advertising — down 3% YoY, dragged by Windows OEM and devices revenue falling 22% YoY.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Spending on building products, led by AI and cloud — up 11% YoY.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Selling and marketing the product line — essentially flat YoY.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day — up 4% YoY.

oneTimers: Non-GAAP results exclude a $207M net gain from investments in OpenAI in Q1 FY27 (vs a $3,086M net loss a year ago) — the reason GAAP net income (+32%) grew much faster than non-GAAP net income (+18%).
verdict: Microsoft grew 19% to $92.3B on Azure's 48% surge, and customers have now committed $677B of future cloud spending — the AI boom is real, and so is the bill to build it.
footerNote: Segments use Microsoft's new FY27 reporting structure.
follow100Note: Kept-as-profit includes +$0.04 of other income per $100 of revenue; the rows add to $100.01 due to rounding.

takeaways.title: AI is the growth engine
takeaways.text: Azure grew 48%, and Microsoft Cloud revenue hit $63.9B — about 69% of all revenue. The growth story is the data centers.

takeaways.title: Customers have already committed
takeaways.text: Commercial remaining performance obligation — contracted future cloud revenue — reached $677B, up 73%. That is years of AI spending already signed.

takeaways.title: The consumer side is shrinking
takeaways.text: Devices & Consumer fell 3%, dragged by Windows OEM and devices revenue down 22%. PCs, Xbox and search ads are now just 17% of revenue — a side business next to the cloud.
